primary_findings: The correction loop worked across all four surgical cases.
Each initial invalid body was remanded with a targeted reason.
Each same-agent correction produced a valid resident body and accepted assembled filing.
The most important semantic case passed: CREATE ui.toast@v3 remained a registry gap after correction and was not repaired into CREATE ui.menu@v1.
This proves a fuller local circuit: body submitted -> remand_required -> corrected body submitted -> accepted_filing.
evidence_boundary: This proves harnessable filing, remand, and correction for declared routes.
It still does not prove broad autonomous natural semantic binding at scale.
Opaque pointer handling here remains discrimination and correction, not full opaque meta-list execution.
recommended_next_iteration: Run hidden-route binding probes where the expected semantic route is not explicitly given in the prompt.
Run a pure opaque sequence probe that checks order, duplicates, unknown IDs, and step-index advancement.
Move stop_posture toward harness ownership in the next harness design, because it is procedural closure law rather than semantic content.
overall_assessment: Probe 013 validates the remand-correction branch of the resident-model meta-loop. The resident model can receive precise remand reasons, correct only the invalid filing surface, and preserve the semantic route under harness validation.
